messages.subject: annotation problem
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am Maite Iriondo and I am studying the transcriptome of Arabidopsis in CAF-1 mutants. 

For my study I have calculated the differentially methylated bases in my data (Arabidopsis with TAIR10 reference) and now I want to link this information with the annotation from a bed file. I trimmed this bed file in order to remove mitochondrial and cloroplast information, and I initially replaced the "chr_" for just the number eg."1". 

When I did this I was not able to read the bed file and got the following error: 
ref<- read.transcript.features("TAIR10_fix.bed")
Error in convert.bed2introns(bed) : this is not a valid bed file

Then I went back to leaving the "chr" signs and I was able to read the file using read.transcript.features(), however, when I wanted to merge the information with my processed data using annotate.WithGenicParts() I got the following error:
>ref<- read.transcript.features("TAIR10_fix2.bed")
> annotate.WithGenicParts(CpG_CG1_diff25, ref)
Warning messages:
1: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  Each of the 2 combined objects has sequence levels not in the other:
  - in 'x': 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  - in 'y': chr1, chr2, chr3, chr4, chr5
  Make sure to always combine/compare objects based on the same reference
  genome (use suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning).
2: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  Each of the 2 combined objects has sequence levels not in the other:
  - in 'x': 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  - in 'y': chr1, chr2, chr3, chr4, chr5
  Make sure to always combine/compare objects based on the same reference
  genome (use suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning).
3: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  Each of the 2 combined objects has sequence levels not in the other:
  - in 'x': 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  - in 'y': chr1, chr2, chr3, chr4, chr5
  Make sure to always combine/compare objects based on the same reference
  genome (use suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning).
4: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  Each of the 2 combined objects has sequence levels not in the other:
  - in 'x': chr1, chr2, chr3, chr4, chr5
  - in 'y': 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  Make sure to always combine/compare objects based on the same reference
  genome (use suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning).
5: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  Each of the 2 combined objects has sequence levels not in the other:
  - in 'x': chr1, chr2, chr3, chr4, chr5
  - in 'y': 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  Make sure to always combine/compare objects based on the same reference
  genome (use suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning).
6: In .Seqinfo.mergexy(x, y) :
  Each of the 2 combined objects has sequence levels not in the other:
  - in 'x': chr1, chr2, chr3, chr4, chr5
  - in 'y': 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  Make sure to always combine/compare objects based on the same reference
  genome (use suppressWarnings() to suppress this warning).
Error in nearest(ranges(g.bed[seqnames(g.bed) == chrs[i], ]), ranges(subject[seqnames(subject) ==  :
  error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'nearest': Error in ranges(g.bed[seqnames(g.bed) == chrs[i], ]) :
  error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'ranges': Error in IRanges:::normalizeSingleBracketSubscript(i, x) :
  subscript contains NAs

I am not able to detect the NAs in my bed file, and right now I cannot get passed this error. I would appreciate if anyone can give me a hint of what could be the problem. 
Could it be that there is some missmatch between the bed file I used and the assembly TAIR10 that I specified in the read() or read.bismark() functions?
Thank you all!

Maite

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: annotation problem
parts:
The problem seems to be that your CpG methylation and annotation file have a different chromosome naming convention, annotation file has "chr" string but not the CpG methylation files. You need to add the "chr" string to your CpG methylation files, so that they both have the same naming convention.

The new version(0.5.7) shouldn't require that the annotation files have the "chr" string in the chromosome names. Previous versions require the "chr" string in the annotation files even though you can read % methylation files without the "chr" string.


Best,
Altuna
